Hi John / Triune CAB,

Following our runbook review last week, we have a critical security hotpatch that needs to be applied to the Private cluster running in your VPC (control-plane and inference nodes). This patch fixes a kernel-level vector that could allow side-channel exposure under very narrow conditions; we recommend applying it to the fleet to meet your compliance timeline.

Key asks:
- Approve a 3-hour maintenance window on Friday 2026-08-13 01:00-04:00 UTC (your local evening) for the hotpatch + verification.
- Approve the network carve-out for the maintenance period: transient routing change + temporary ephemeral VLAN and host-level firewall lock to isolate patched hosts from production traffic during validation.
- Authorize the hotpatch escrow: ability for Redwood to temporarily override version pinning on up to 10% of nodes for emergency micro-patches, with immediate rollback if any functional regression is detected.

Attached: triune_hotpatch_plan_v1.pdf (detailed steps), network-carveout-diagram.png (topology).

We propose the following rollback SLA: 30 minutes to rollback to pinned version on any affected node, and full fleet rollback target of 2 hours if a systemic issue is observed. We will run automated pre-checks (smoke tests, synthetic inference at 95th percentile load) and a staged canary (1 -> 5 -> 20% nodes).

Please confirm whether the CAB can approve the window and the escrow override today so we can schedule the CAB change. If the proposed window doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks,

John — quick technical clarifications to include in the one-page attestation for your CAB: feel free to paste these into the doc.

1) No persistent BGP/route changes. The carve-out uses a transient host-level routing shim and ephemeral VLAN that is removed at the end of the validation window. Control plane endpoints remain reachable over the same EIP; we only alter host-to-host east-west paths for the canary group.

2) Escrow override mechanics: Redwood will create a signed change bundle per node (timestamped, audit-signed) that unpins the model runtime package for that node only. The bundle is stored in our audit log and we provide you with the bundle IDs and hashes ahead of the window. We will not change image tags in your central registry. The override is node-scoped and auto-reverts at the end of the window unless validated. All actions are logged to the customer KMS-backed audit trail.

3) Smoke tests: we run the following before promoting a canary stage — startup health checks, KV cache warmup verification, synthetic inference at 10qps and 95th-percentile latency sampling, end-to-end metrics push to your Prometheus endpoint, and correctness regression tests against your pinned prompts (we include prompt set ids in the runbook).

4) Rollback plan: per-node rollback uses a fast-path snapshot rollback (we keep a warm golden image) and rejoin is orchestrated with sequence numbers to avoid split-kv states; target median per-node rollback time is 18 minutes in our canary rehearsals, worst-case 30 minutes. Full fleet rollback (if escalation) estimated 90-120 minutes depending on queued requests; we throttle to maintain control-plane stability.

5) Safety gates: if 3 or more nodes in the first 20% show >5% correctness degradation or latency beat threshold, we abort and initiate the rollback. Diagnosis hooks will dump kv-cache metrics and tail telemetry for the incident channel.

I've attached a brief diagram (network-carveout-diagram.png) and referenced the runbook section IDs that map to each step in the one-pager.

If Triune CAB wants, we can run a preflight dry run in your staging VPC tomorrow at the same window to validate procedure; this typically takes ~45 minutes.

-Karthik
